了.etymology: 了 liǎo “to understand; can” — the same wrapped-up child as the particle le; said as a full syllable it still means to bring something to an end, so 了解 is to understand it and 不了 is to be unable to finish it.

地.etymology: 地 de “adverb marker” — 土 tǔ “earth” plus phonetic 也 yě is dì “ground”; with no stress after an adjective, the same character only marks an adverb (慢慢地 màn màn de “slowly”).

觉.etymology: 觉 jiào “to sleep” — 见 jiàn “see” plus the phonetic of 学 xué gives jué “to feel, to wake”; jiào is the sleep in 睡觉, the state that waking comes out of. Simplified 覺 → 觉.

着.etymology: 着 zháo “to touch; to catch” — from 著 “to put on, to come into contact”; that contact gives 着火 “catch fire” and 着急 “anxiety catches you,” while unstressed zhe only marks an action still going on.

便.etymology: 便 pián “cheap” — 亻 rén “person” and 更 gēng “change” give biàn “convenient”; the same word, said pián yi, narrowed from “a convenient bargain” to “cheap.”

和.etymology: 和 huo “mild” — unstressed 和 after 暖 nuǎn or 软 ruǎn softens the adjective, as in 暖和 “nice and warm” and 软和 “soft.” Stressed hé is “and; harmony.”

曲.etymology: 曲 qǔ “tune” — the warped-board picture gives qū “bent”; a melody was taken as a line that bends, so qǔ is a tune or song (乐曲, 歌曲).

背.etymology: 背 bēi “to carry” — 北 běi pictured two people standing back to back, and ⺼ ròu “flesh” marks the body; bèi is that back, and bēi is to carry a load on it.
